description: Minimal hybrid PDF with vector header text overlaid on scanned body content

source.generation_method: Generated via tests/fixtures/hybrid/hybrid-001-generator.py using raw PDF construction: vector text (Helvetica, 14pt, top ~120 pts) with 1-bit grayscale image XObject (scanned body, bottom 672 pts)

hybrid_behavior.vector_regions: Page header (rows 0-1 of 8x8 grid, columns 0-7): Company name 'ACME Corp', report title 'Annual Report 2024'
hybrid_behavior.scanned_regions: Page body (rows 1-7 of 8x8 grid, columns 0-7): 1-bit grayscale image XObject with horizontal line pattern simulating scanned text
hybrid_behavior.overlap_description: Clean vertical separation with vector header in top ~15% and scanned image in bottom ~85%

grid_cell_coverage.hybrid_cell_locations: Row 1 (the boundary row between header and body) contains both vector text cells above and image content below

classification_challenges: Minimal PDF size (1.2 KB) may be atypical compared to real-world hybrid PDFs
Clean regional separation may cause classifier to treat as separate Vector + Scanned regions rather than unified Hybrid page
Boundary detection: accurate identification of transition from vector to image content
Image is 1-bit grayscale only, lacking color complexity of typical scans
Tests non-overlapping merge rule behavior when regions are cleanly separated vertically
test_focus: Header extraction precision: ensuring vector header is not subjected to OCR
OCR on body only without interference from vector header
Minimal fixture performance: tests classification on very small files
notes: Synthetic minimal fixture designed to test hybrid classification at the smallest viable scale. Vector header content is selectable text (Helvetica font), body content is 1-bit image XObject with horizontal line pattern simulating scanned text. This fixture tests the fundamental hybrid detection capability: identifying pages that contain both vector and image content types. The clean vertical separation makes this a baseline case before testing more complex overlapping scenarios.
